title: My family's secret group chat
author: Storytime
hook: I found out my family has a group chat without me. It's called Operation Sam. I'm Sam.
story: Last weekend, I borrowed my mom's tablet to look up a recipe. A notification popped up. Group chat. Operation Sam. Eleven members. My parents, my sisters, my aunts, even my grandma. Everyone except me. I opened it. Obviously. The first message was from my sister, three months ago. Has anyone else noticed Sam disappears every Sunday at six in the morning? Then my dad. I checked his location. He's at an address across town. Every week. Then my aunt. He's been so secretive. Then my grandma. I think it's a cult. Then my mom. We need an intervention. They have a whole plan. Thanksgiving. After dessert. My sister booked a therapist to come over. My aunt printed pamphlets. Here's the truth. Every Sunday at six, I volunteer at an animal shelter. I walk the dogs nobody wants to adopt. I didn't tell anyone, because last year I said I wanted a dog, and my whole family laughed and said I can't even keep a plant alive. Now I'm adopting one of them. A three legged senior beagle named Biscuit. I'm picking him up the day before Thanksgiving. So, do I let them do the intervention, and bring Biscuit?
caption: Operation Sam was not what they thought 🐶 #storytime
sound: a sneaky detective theme that turns sweet at very low volume
why: Discovering a family group chat without you is trending, the cult theory is funny escalation, the shelter twist is wholesome, and bringing Biscuit to the intervention invites comments.

title: My husband invited his ex-wife to Thanksgiving
author: Storytime
hook: My husband asked if his ex-wife could come to our Thanksgiving. I said no. Then my stepdaughter told me why he asked.
story: I married my husband Mark four years ago. He has a daughter, Ava, who's fifteen. Ava's mom, Diane, and I have always been polite, but distant. Last week, Mark asked me, would you be okay if Diane came to Thanksgiving this year? I said no. Honestly, a little too fast. I said, it's my first year hosting your whole family, and I don't want it to be weird. He just nodded and dropped it. Two days later, Ava came into the kitchen while I was making a grocery list. She said, I need to tell you something, but Mom doesn't want anyone to know. Diane is sick. She started treatment in October. Her family lives overseas, and she was going to spend Thanksgiving alone, in a hospital bed, because she was too proud to ask. Mark asked for Ava, not for himself. I felt terrible. So I called Diane myself. She cried on the phone. Then she said, only if I can bring my famous pecan pie. Now she's coming. But my mother-in-law found out, and says it's completely inappropriate to have the ex at the table. Is it?
caption: I said no too fast 🥧 #storytime
sound: a warm, emotional acoustic guitar at very low volume
why: Thanksgiving guest list fights are peaking, the quick no makes viewers relate then reconsider, the stepdaughter's reveal is emotional, and the is it inappropriate question splits opinions.

title: She saved twelve seats at the school concert
author: Storytime
hook: At my son's school holiday concert, a woman saved twelve seats in the front row with coats. I moved them.
story: My son is seven, and it was his first winter concert. He had one line. One. He practiced it for a month. I got to the school forty-five minutes early to get a good seat. The entire front row was covered in coats. Twelve seats. And one woman sitting in the middle, guarding them. I asked if they were all taken. She said, yes, they're for my people. Thirty minutes later, still nobody. The gym was packed. Parents standing in the back. My son was going to be on the far end of the stage. So I moved two coats to the floor, and sat down with my wife. The woman gave me the coldest look I've ever seen. Five minutes before the concert, the doors opened. In came twelve elderly people, walking slowly, some with canes, one in a wheelchair. They were from the retirement home across the street. Every year, the school invites them. That woman organizes it. They'd been stuck at the crosswalk. I stood up so fast I knocked my chair over. Then I gave my seat to a ninety year old man named Frank. Frank was the best audience member there. But I still feel awful. Should I apologize to her?
caption: the coats were for them 🎄 #storytime
sound: a gentle school bell melody with a heartwarming swell at very low volume
why: Seat saving is a hot debate topic, viewers side with the narrator at first, the retirement home twist flips the villain, and the apology question gets lots of comments.
